# tag: geo.old-capital
what was the capital of brazil before brasilia | did rio used to be the capital of brazil | when did brasilia become the capital => Rio de Janeiro was Brazil's capital until 1960, when the new planned city of Brasília became the capital.
what was the capital of nigeria before abuja | did lagos used to be the capital of nigeria | when did abuja become the capital of nigeria => Lagos was Nigeria's capital until 1991, when the government moved to Abuja, a planned city in the middle of the country.
what was the capital of pakistan before islamabad | did karachi used to be the capital of pakistan | when did islamabad become the capital => Karachi was Pakistan's first capital. Islamabad was built in the 1960s to become the new capital.
what was the capital of turkey before ankara | did istanbul used to be the capital of turkey | when did ankara become the capital => Istanbul was the capital of the Ottoman Empire. Ankara became the capital of the new Republic of Turkey in 1923.
what was the capital of japan before tokyo | did kyoto used to be the capital of japan | when did tokyo become the capital of japan => Kyoto was Japan's imperial capital for more than 1,000 years. The emperor moved to Tokyo in 1868 and 1869.
what was the capital of russia before moscow | did st petersburg used to be the capital of russia | when did moscow become the capital of russia => St. Petersburg was Russia's capital from 1712 to 1918, when the government moved back to Moscow.
what was the capital of kazakhstan before astana | did almaty used to be the capital of kazakhstan | when did astana become the capital => Almaty was Kazakhstan's capital until 1997, when the capital moved north to Astana.
what was the capital of myanmar before naypyidaw | did yangon used to be the capital of myanmar | when did naypyidaw become the capital => Yangon was Myanmar's capital until 2005 and 2006, when the government moved to the new city of Naypyidaw.
what was the capital of germany before berlin | did bonn used to be the capital of germany | when did berlin become the capital of germany again => Bonn was the capital of West Germany. After Germany reunited in 1990, Berlin became the capital, and the government moved there by 1999.
what was the capital of australia before canberra | did melbourne used to be the capital of australia | when did canberra become the capital => Melbourne was the temporary home of Australia's government from 1901 to 1927, while Canberra was being built.
what was the capital of the united states before washington dc | did new york used to be the capital of the united states => New York City was the first capital under the Constitution, in 1789 and 1790. Philadelphia was the capital from 1790 to 1800, and then Washington, DC.
what was the capital of belize before belmopan | when did belmopan become the capital => Belize City was the capital until 1970, when the government moved inland to Belmopan after a hurricane flooded Belize City in 1961.
what was the capital of malawi before lilongwe | did zomba used to be the capital of malawi => Zomba was Malawi's capital until 1975, when the capital moved to Lilongwe.
what was the capital of ivory coast before yamoussoukro | did abidjan used to be the capital of ivory coast => Abidjan was Ivory Coast's capital until 1983, when Yamoussoukro became the official capital. Most government offices are still in Abidjan.
what was the capital of tanzania before dodoma | did dar es salaam used to be the capital of tanzania => Dar es Salaam was Tanzania's capital. Dodoma was chosen as the new capital in 1973, and the government finished moving there in the 2010s and 2020s.
# tag: geo.country-nickname
why is italy called the boot | which country is shaped like a boot | what country looks like a boot | italy boot shape => Italy is shaped like a high-heeled boot, with the island of Sicily looking like a ball at its toe.
why is france called the hexagon | which country is called l'hexagone | france hexagon => France is nicknamed l'Hexagone, the hexagon, because mainland France has roughly six sides.
which country is long and thin | what country is the skinniest | why is chile so long and thin => Chile is one of the longest, thinnest countries in the world. It's about 4,300 kilometers (2,700 miles) long but on average only about 175 kilometers (110 miles) wide.
# tag: geo.former-name
is turkey now called turkiye | why did turkey change its name | what is turkiye => Turkey asked the world to call it Türkiye in 2022, and the United Nations now uses that name. Many people still say Turkey in English.
is czechia the same as czech republic | why is it called czechia now | czechia or czech republic => Czechia is the short name of the Czech Republic. The country made the short name official in 2016, and both names are correct.
what countries were in the soviet union | what is the ussr => The Soviet Union (USSR) was a huge communist country from 1922 to 1991. When it broke up, it became 15 countries, including Russia, Ukraine, Kazakhstan, Georgia and the three Baltic states.
what countries were in yugoslavia | what happened to yugoslavia => Yugoslavia was a country in southeastern Europe that broke up in the 1990s. Its parts are now Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Kosovo.
what was czechoslovakia | what happened to czechoslovakia | when did czechoslovakia split => Czechoslovakia peacefully split into two countries, the Czech Republic (Czechia) and Slovakia, on 1 January 1993. People called it the Velvet Divorce.
what was east germany | when did east and west germany unite | why was germany split in two => After World War II, Germany was split into West Germany and communist East Germany. They reunited on 3 October 1990.
what is the newest country | youngest country in the world => South Sudan became independent from Sudan on 9 July 2011. As of 2025, it's the newest country recognized by most of the world.
# tag: geo.name-origin
what does stan mean in country names | why do so many countries end in stan | what does the stan in kazakhstan mean => The ending -stan comes from Persian and means land of or place of. So Uzbekistan means land of the Uzbeks.
why is england called england | where does the name england come from | what does england mean => England means land of the Angles, a Germanic people who settled there about 1,500 years ago.
why is scotland called scotland | where does the name scotland come from => Scotland is named after the Scoti, a Latin name the Romans used for Gaelic-speaking people from Ireland who settled there.
why is wales called wales | where does the name wales come from | what does cymru mean => Wales comes from an old English word meaning foreigners. The Welsh call their country Cymru, which means fellow countrymen.
why is greenland called greenland if its icy | why is greenland called greenland | where does the name greenland come from => The Viking Erik the Red named it Greenland around 985 AD, probably to make it sound nice so people would move there. It's mostly covered in ice.
why is america called america | where does the name america come from | who was america named after => America is named after Amerigo Vespucci, an Italian explorer who realized the Americas were a new continent. A German mapmaker, Martin Waldseemüller, put the name on a map in 1507.
why is it called the united kingdom | what does united kingdom mean => The United Kingdom unites four countries, England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, under one king or queen. Its full name is the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland.
why is the pacific called the pacific | what does pacific mean => Ferdinand Magellan named it Mar Pacífico, peaceful sea, in 1520, because it was calm when his ships sailed into it.
why is the atlantic called the atlantic | where does the name atlantic come from => The Atlantic is named after Atlas, a Titan in Greek myths who held up the sky.
why is the red sea called the red sea | how did the red sea get its name => No one knows for sure. It may come from red algae that sometimes grow in it, or from an old way of naming directions by colors, where red meant south.
why is the black sea called the black sea | how did the black sea get its name => No one knows for sure. It may come from an old way of naming directions by colors, where black meant north, or from its dark, stormy look.
